question: A truck covers a fixed distance in 40 minutes at an average speed of 180 km/h. Due to construction, it needs to be rerouted, increasing the distance by 10%. If the truck needs to arrive at its destination on time (i.e., in 40 minutes), what should its new average speed be in km/h?
solution:
**Given:**

Fixed distance covered in 40 minutes = Distance 1

Average speed for Distance 1 = 180 km/h

New distance = Distance 1 + 10% of Distance 1

Required time = 40 minutes = 40 ÷ 60 hours = 2/3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

New Average Speed = New Distance ÷ Required Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance 1 = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance 1 = 180 × (2/3)

⇒ Distance 1 = 120 km

⇒ New Distance = Distance 1 + 10% of Distance 1

⇒ New Distance = 120 + (10/100) × 120

⇒ New Distance = 120 + 12

⇒ New Distance = 132 km

⇒ New Average Speed = New Distance ÷ Required Time

⇒ New Average Speed = 132 ÷ (2/3)

⇒ New Average Speed = 132 × (3/2)

⇒ New Average Speed = 198 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 198 km/h.**
